root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画、染色」的施事名词 pictor，经古法语 peintor 进入英语，14 世纪初指画家，约 1400 年兼指油漆工。指船缆的 painter 为同形异源词，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses distinguish the fine artist from the trade worker, then split by subject, medium, historical role, amateur status, sign work and workshop division of labour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把纯艺术家与行业工人分开，再按题材、媒介、历史角色、业余身份、招牌工作与工坊分工细分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand arranges colour on a canvas and flattens colour on a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只手在画布上安排颜色，也在墙上把颜色铺平。

branches.en: THE PICTURE MAKER: the artist whose product is an image.
branches.cn: 作画者：产物是一幅图像的艺术家。

branches.en: THE SURFACE COATER: the same agent noun in the building trade.
branches.cn: 表面涂覆者：同一施事名词在建筑行业中的用法。

branches.en: SUBJECT: identity narrowed to what is depicted.
branches.cn: 题材：身份被收窄到所描绘之物。

branches.en: MEDIUM AND HISTORY: the material mastered, then the figure in the catalogue.
branches.cn: 媒介与历史：所精通的材料，然后是图录中的人物。

branches.en: ROLES AROUND THE CRAFT: amateur, sign worker and workshop hand.
branches.cn: 手艺周边的角色：业余者、招牌工与工坊画师。

intro.en: Painter is a verb stem plus the agent suffix -er; the stem's Latin ancestor builds a whole family of images, materials and actions.
intro.cn: painter 是动词词干加施事后缀 -er；其词干的拉丁祖先构成一整族图像、材料与动作词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pictor is the direct model; pingere also yields picture, pigment, depict and pictorial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pictor 是直接模板；pingere 还给出 picture、pigment、depict 与 pictorial。

items.structure: Old French peindre, from Latin pingere

items.example: Painter follows the pattern of builder.
items.exampleCN: painter 沿用了 builder 的模式。

items.example: The painter signed the lower corner.
The sky is handled in a painterly way.
items.exampleCN: 天空以绘画式手法处理。

items.example: The painted cloth hung behind the altar.

items.exampleCN: 壁带描绘一支游行队伍。

items.example: The pigment is ground by hand.
The picture is older than the frame.

definition_zh: 一双；一对；一对人；一对动物；配对
definition_en: two things or people that belong together, or to put two such things together
core_image: 两只一模一样的手套并排放着，指尖对着指尖
scene: 清晨的门口，两只沾了泥的靴子被人并排放好，鞋尖朝外。She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
sceneCN: 这里 pair 是「一双、一对配套的东西」（第 1 个义项：成对使用的两件物品）；句意是她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。图中可辨识的物件：门口的靴子、泥点、手套。

pos.zh: 一双；一对；一对人；一对动物

derivatives.zh: 由 pair 加 -ed 构成，义为「成对的；配对的」
由 pair 加 -ing 构成，义为「配对；搭配」
由 pair 加表示否定的前缀 un- 与 -ed 构成，义为「未配对的」
由 pair 与 -wise 复合而成，义为「成对地；两两之间地」

senses.title: Two things that go together
senses.definition: two things of the same kind that are used together or look the same
senses.definitionCN: 同一种类、搭配使用或看起来相配的两件东西
senses.example: She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。
senses.why: Latin paria were equal things, so the word starts from two items that answer each other, not from any particular object.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 paria 指「相等的东西」，所以这个词的起点是两件彼此对应的物品，而不是某种特定的东西。

senses.title: Two people linked together
senses.definition: two people who are connected by love, work or a shared activity
senses.definitionCN: 因感情、工作或共同活动而连在一起的两个人
senses.example: The pair have worked in the same lab for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个人在同一间实验室共事了十年。
senses.why: Since paria means equals, the word easily moves from matching objects to two people who are matched in some role.
senses.whyCN: 既然 paria 意为「相等之物」，这个词就很容易从相配的物品转到在某种角色上相配的两个人。

senses.title: Two animals kept together
senses.definition: a male and a female animal, or two animals of the same kind, kept together
senses.definitionCN: 养在一起的一雌一雄，或同种的两只动物
senses.example: The farm bought a pair of geese for the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 农场为池塘买了一对鹅。
senses.why: Breeding needs two, and the old sense of equal things fits a male and female kept together for mating.
senses.whyCN: 繁殖需要两个，而「相等之物」的老义正好贴合为交配而养在一起的一雄一雌。

senses.title: To put two things together
senses.definition: to join two things or people so that they form a matching set or a working team
senses.definitionCN: 把两件东西或两个人组合起来，成为相配的一套或一个搭档
senses.example: Students were paired by level for the speaking test.
senses.exampleCN: 口语考试按水平把学生两人一组配对。
senses.why: Once a pair names a set of two, the verb simply performs the action of making that set exist.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pair 指「两个组成的一套」，动词就是让这样一套真正形成的动作。

intro.en: Pair comes from Latin words for equal things, which passed through French and came to name any two items that answer each other.
intro.cn: pair 来自拉丁语中表示「相等之物」的词，经法语传来，后来指任何彼此对应的两件东西。

items.en: Par meant equal or a match, and it is the stem behind a family of words about being level.
items.cn: par 意为相等的、对等的，是整族表示「持平」的词背后的词干。

items.en: The neuter plural paria named equal things taken together, which is the form the noun needed.
items.cn: 中性复数 paria 指放在一起的相等之物，正好是名词所需的形式。

items.en: Old French paire kept the sense of a set of two matching things.
items.cn: 古法语 paire 保留了「相配的两件成一套」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pair widened from matching objects to couples, partners and animals kept together.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pair 从相配的物品扩展到伴侣、搭档和养在一起的动物。

items.en: Modern English uses pair as a noun for any matched two and as a verb for the act of matching.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pair 用作名词指任何相配的两个，也用作动词指配对的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives of the Latin stem for equal; the near-meaning group collects words for twos and partners.
note.cn: 形近组收「相等」这一拉丁词干的同族词；近义组收表示「两个」与「搭档」的词。

entries.definition: An equal level or standard, as in the phrase on par with.
entries.definitionCN: 相等的水平或标准，如短语 on par with。

entries.definition: The state of being equal in rank or value.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或价值相等的状态。

entries.definition: To set two things side by side to see how they differ.
entries.definitionCN: 把两样东西放在一起看差异。

entries.definition: To cut away the outer skin of something; it is only close in sound, and its source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 削去外皮；只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Two people together, or two of the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 在一起的两个人，或同类的两个。

entries.definition: Two people who perform or work together.
entries.definitionCN: 一起表演或工作的两个人。

entries.definition: One of two things that go well together.
entries.definitionCN: 相配的两件中的一件。

entries.definition: One of two children born at the same time, or one of a matching set.
entries.definitionCN: 双胞胎之一，或相配一对中的一个。

normalIntro.en: Pair rests on a Latin word for equal, so the whole family is about two things that stand level with each other.
normalIntro.cn: pair 依托拉丁语中表示「相等」的词，所以整族词都围绕「彼此持平的两样东西」。

normal.en: Latin par means equal, and paria is its plural for equal things, which is exactly what a pair is.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 par 意为相等，paria 是它的复数，指相等之物，正是一对的意思。

normal.en: Parity, par and compare all keep the equal part of the same stem.
normal.cn: parity、par 和 compare 都保留着同一词干里「相等」的那部分。

normal.en: Pair up adds a particle that turns the noun into the action of forming a set.
normal.cn: pair up 加上一个小词，就把名词变成「组成一套」的动作。

normal.en: In pairs uses the plural to mean two at a time, a pattern that appears in classrooms and queues.
normal.cn: in pairs 用复数表示「一次两个」，课堂和排队时都常见。

normal.en: A pair of shoes works because the two shoes answer each other, not because there are simply two shoes.
normal.cn: 一双鞋之所以成双，是因为两只鞋彼此对应，而不是因为刚好有两只鞋。

abstract.en: Two equal things need each other to be a pair, which is why the word carries a quiet idea of balance.
abstract.cn: 两个相等之物要彼此依存才成对，所以这个词暗暗带着平衡的意味。

abstract.en: Pairing is a way of organising the world by twos, from shoes to lab partners.
abstract.cn: 配对是把世界按「两个」来整理的一种方式，从鞋子到实验搭档都一样。

abstract.en: A word born from equality reminds us that a pair only works when both sides count.
abstract.cn: 一个从「相等」生出的词提醒人：一对要成立，两边都得算数。

examples.en: She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
examples.cn: 她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。

examples.en: Students were paired by level for the speaking test.
examples.cn: 口语考试按水平把学生两人一组配对。

examples.en: The two socks do not make a pair.
examples.cn: 这两只袜子配不成一双。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩尔」——把两只配好，正好配成一对；pair 是一双。

root: 拉丁语 par（相等的）之中性复数 paria 指「相等之物」，经古法语 paire 进入英语；同族词多与「相等、对等」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things standing equal to each other; the senses spread to objects used together, linked people, animals kept as a pair, and the act of matching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是彼此持平的两样东西；义项扩展到配套使用的物品、连在一起的两个人、成对饲养的动物，以及配对的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical gloves laid side by side, fingertip to fingertip.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只一模一样的手套并排放着，指尖对着指尖。

branches.en: two shoes waiting at the door toe to toe
branches.cn: 两只鞋并排等在门口，鞋尖对着鞋尖

branches.en: two lab partners sharing one bench
branches.cn: 两个实验搭档共用一张台子

branches.en: a goose following its mate to the pond
branches.cn: 一只鹅跟着伴侣走向池塘

branches.en: names on a list being joined two by two
branches.cn: 名单上的名字被两个两个连起来

branches.en: a word for equality used for gloves and for people
branches.cn: 一个表示相等的词，既用于手套也用于人

intro.en: The word grows from a Latin stem for equal, its plural form, and English endings that turn it into an adjective, a noun and a verb.
intro.cn: 这个词从表示「相等」的拉丁词干和它的复数形式生长出来，再加上英语词尾，变成形容词、名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: Par, the Latin adjective for equal, and its neuter plural paria stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 par（相等的）及其中性复数 paria 是英语这个词背后的来源。

derivatives.zh: 由 pair 加 -ed 构成，指成对的
由 pair 加 -ing 构成，指配对
由 un- 与 paired 构成，指未配对的

definition_zh: 宫殿；王宫；主教府；豪华宅邸；大型公共文化建筑
definition_en: the official residence of a king, queen, bishop or other high dignitary, or any very large and grand building
core_image: 一道正门通向铺石大院，院后是层层抬高的殿堂，每一层都比前一层更不容外人进入
scene: 铁门后是铺石大院，台阶一层层通向正殿。The palace opens its state rooms to visitors only two months a year.
sceneCN: 这里 palace 指「君主或高级显要的官邸」（第 1 个义项：王宫、宫殿）；句意为这座王宫每年只有两个月向访客开放国事厅。图中可辨识物件：铁门、铺石大院、台阶、正殿；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 豪华大宅；大型公共建筑

derivatives.zh: 宫殿般的；宏伟的
行宫领地；普法尔茨伯爵领地
宫廷政变
宫廷革命
意大利式府邸

senses.title: The residence of a ruler
senses.definition: the official home and ceremonial centre of a king, queen or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 国王、女王或皇帝的官邸与礼仪中心
senses.example: The palace balcony faces the wide avenue where crowds gather.
senses.exampleCN: 王宫的阳台朝向人群聚集的宽阔大道。
senses.why: the word began as the name of one hill in Rome, then of the emperor's house on it, and finally of any ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是罗马一座山的名字，随后指山上皇帝的宅邸，最后泛指任何君主的宅邸。

senses.title: A bishop's residence
senses.definition: the official residence of a bishop or archbishop, often beside the cathedral
senses.definitionCN: 主教或大主教的官邸，常位于主教座堂旁
senses.example: The archbishop's palace shares a wall with the cathedral garden.
senses.exampleCN: 大主教府与主教座堂的花园共用一道墙。
senses.why: bishops held princely authority in many periods, so their houses took the same word as a king's.
senses.whyCN: 在许多时期主教握有诸侯般的权柄，因此他们的宅邸与国王用同一个词。

senses.title: A very grand private house
senses.definition: a private mansion large and ornate enough to seem royal
senses.definitionCN: 大到与华丽到看上去像王室居所的私人宅邸
senses.example: The merchant built a palace of brick beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那位商人在河边建了一座砖砌豪宅。
senses.why: wealth copies the forms of power, so a rich man's house borrows the name of a ruler's house.
senses.whyCN: 财富会模仿权力的形式，因此富人的宅邸借用了君主居所的名字。

senses.title: A public palace of culture
senses.titleCN: 文化宫等大型公共建筑
senses.definition: a large state-built hall for culture, sport or exhibitions, common in former socialist countries
senses.definitionCN: 国家兴建的大型文化、体育或展览场馆，在旧社会主义国家常见
senses.example: The palace of culture has a theatre, a library and a swimming pool.
senses.exampleCN: 这座文化宫里有剧场、图书馆和游泳池。
senses.why: the state took the prestige of the palace and gave it to public leisure, so the word became civic.
senses.whyCN: 国家把宫殿的声望转给公共休闲，因此这个词变得市政化。

senses.title: Any lavish place
senses.definition: a building or room remarkable for comfort, size and expense
senses.definitionCN: 以舒适、宽敞与昂贵著称的建筑或房间
senses.example: The old cinema was a palace of red velvet and gilded plaster.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老电影院是一座红丝绒与镀金灰泥的宫殿。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the splendour of the original, dropping the ruler entirely.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只保留原义的富丽，把君主完全去掉了。

senses.title: The court as a government
senses.definition: the ruler's household and advisers, treated as a political actor
senses.definitionCN: 君主的家臣与顾问群体，被当作一个政治行为者
senses.example: The palace denied that the minister had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 王室方面否认那位大臣已被免职。
senses.why: reporters say 'the palace' when they mean the household that speaks for the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 记者说「王室」时，指的是替君主发声的那套家臣体系。

senses.title: The Palatine hill in Rome
senses.titleCN: 罗马帕拉蒂尼山上的宫殿
senses.definition: the imperial residence on the Palatine hill, whose name became the general word
senses.definitionCN: 帕拉蒂尼山上的皇帝居所，其名字成为通名
senses.example: The ruins of the palace overlook the forum.
senses.exampleCN: 宫殿废墟俯瞰着广场。
senses.why: one hill's name spread until every ruler's house in Europe carried it.
senses.whyCN: 一座山的名字扩散开来，直到欧洲每位君主的宅邸都带上了它。

senses.title: A movie palace
senses.definition: a large, lavishly decorated cinema of the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪初那种装饰华丽的大型电影院
senses.example: The movie palace seats two thousand under a painted sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这座电影宫在画出来的天空下可坐两千人。
senses.why: early cinemas sold an evening of luxury, so they named themselves after the most luxurious building they knew.
senses.whyCN: 早期影院卖的是一晚的奢华，因此用他们所知最奢华的建筑来命名自己。

intro.en: Palace is a place name before it is a building word: the Palatine hill in Rome gave its name to the emperor's house and then to grand houses everywhere. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: palace 先是地名，后才是建筑词：罗马的帕拉蒂尼山把名字给了皇帝的宅邸，再给了各地的宏大宅邸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Palatium was the name of one of Rome's seven hills, where Augustus and later emperors built their residences.
items.cn: Palatium 是罗马七座山之一的名字，奥古斯都及后来的皇帝在此营建居所。

items.en: Because the emperor's house stood on that hill, the hill's name became a word for the house itself.
items.cn: 由于皇帝的宅邸立在那座山上，山名便成了指宅邸本身的词。

items.en: Old French palais carried the word into English, where it first named a royal residence.
items.cn: 古法语 palais 把该词带入英语，最初指王室居所。

items.en: In the Middle Ages the word widened to bishops' houses and then to any exceptionally grand town house.
items.cn: 中世纪时该词扩展到主教府，再扩展到任何格外宏大的城中宅邸。

items.en: In the twentieth century states built palaces of culture and workers' clubs, giving the word a public meaning.
items.cn: 二十世纪国家兴建文化宫与工人俱乐部，使这个词带上公共含义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the origin of the hill name Palatium is disputed; a link to a shepherd god or to a word for a stake has been suggested, but neither is demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：山名 Palatium 的来源有争议；有人提出与牧神有关，或与表示「木桩」的词有关，但两者都未得到证实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like palace or share its grand-house field but differ in origin; group two holds other grand residences.
note.cn: 第一组是与 palace 形近或同属「宏大宅邸」语义场、但来源不同的词；第二组是其他显赫居所。

entries.definition: Like a palace in size and splendour; it describes a quality and never names a building type.
entries.definitionCN: 在体量与富丽上像宫殿；描述一种性质，从不指建筑类型。

entries.definition: The domain of a count palatine, an official with royal powers in a border region; it names land and office.
entries.definitionCN: 宫廷伯爵的领地，指在边境地区拥有王权的官员辖区；指土地与职衔。

entries.definition: An Italian town house of a noble family; English borrowed it for a specific Mediterranean type.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利贵族家族的城中宅邸；英语借来表示一种特定的地中海类型。

entries.definition: A seizure of power by insiders close to the ruler; the phrase uses palace as the seat of power, not as architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 由君主身边内部人发动的夺权；短语把 palace 当作权力中心，而非建筑。

entries.definition: A fortified residence; it stresses defence, while a palace stresses display and administration.
entries.definitionCN: 设防的居所，强调防御；而 palace 强调展示与治理。

entries.definition: A very large private house; it lacks the royal or episcopal rank that palace implies.
entries.definitionCN: 极大型的私人住宅；缺少 palace 所含的王室或主教等级。

entries.definition: The neutral word for an official home, used when rank should not be emphasized.
entries.definitionCN: 指官邸的中性词，用于不宜强调等级时。

entries.definition: A French country house or estate; it combines castle and country house associations.
entries.definitionCN: 法国的乡间宅邸或庄园，兼有城堡与乡居宅邸的联想。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real hill name, the real rank words and the real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的山名、真实的等级词与真实的复合词。

normal.en: One hill in Rome gave its name to every royal house in Europe.
normal.cn: 罗马的一座山，把名字给了欧洲每一座王室宅邸。

normal.en: The family runs palace, palatial, palatinate, palazzo, palace coup.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 palace、palatial、palatinate、palazzo、palace coup。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: royal palace, archbishop's palace, palace of culture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：王宫、大主教府、文化宫。

normal.en: Rank decides the word: a bishop's house and a king's house can both be palaces.
normal.cn: 等级决定用词：主教的宅邸与国王的宅邸都可以叫 palace。

normal.en: The movie palace sold luxury by borrowing the most luxurious name available.
normal.cn: 电影宫借用了当时最奢华的名字来售卖奢华。

abstract.en: Picture a house that has swallowed a whole hill and now wears its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子吞下了整座山，并把山名穿在身上。

abstract.en: Picture a private hallway so long that a guest needs a map to reach the dining room.
abstract.cn: 想象一条私家长廊，长到客人要拿地图才找得到餐厅。

abstract.en: Picture a cinema whose ceiling is painted as a night sky, so the audience sits outdoors indoors.
abstract.cn: 想象一座影院把天花板画成夜空，观众于是在室内坐在户外。

examples.en: The palace was opened as a museum after the monarchy ended.
examples.cn: 君主制结束后，这座王宫被改为博物馆开放。

examples.en: The archbishop's palace dates from the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 大主教府始建于十二世纪。

examples.en: They restored the movie palace instead of demolishing it.
examples.cn: 他们修复了那座电影宫，而没有将其拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: Palatium（罗马帕拉蒂尼山）→ 山上皇帝宅邸 → 宫殿、豪华宅邸

root: 拉丁 Palatium 原为罗马七丘之一的名字，因皇帝宅邸建于其上而转指宫殿；经古法语 palais 入英语。山名本身的来源不确定。英语 palace。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one address: a ruler's house on a hill becomes a bishop's house, a rich man's house, a public hall, a metaphor, a government, a ruin and a cinema.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个住处展开：山上的君主宅邸成为主教府、富商大宅、公共厅堂、比喻、政府、废墟与影院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gate, courtyard, stair and inner hall, each layer admitting fewer people than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：门、院、阶、内殿，每一层允许进入的人都比前一层更少。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL HOUSE: the hill name became the emperor's residence, and that residence became the general word.
branches.cn: 最初的宅邸：山名成为皇帝居所之名，那座居所又成为通名。

branches.en: PRINCELY CLERGY: a bishop's house takes the royal word because bishops held princely power.
branches.cn: 诸侯般的主教：主教府沿用王室用词，因为主教握有诸侯般的权力。

branches.en: WEALTH COPIES POWER: a merchant's mansion and a lavish hotel borrow palace's splendour without a ruler.
branches.cn: 财富模仿权力：富商豪宅与豪华旅馆借走了 palace 的富丽，却不要君主。

branches.en: PUBLIC SPLENDOUR: the state builds palaces of culture, and cinemas call themselves movie palaces.
branches.cn: 公共的富丽：国家兴建文化宫，影院则自称电影宫。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: the building's name moves to the people who speak for the ruler.
branches.cn: 家臣体系：建筑之名转到替君主发声的那群人身上。

intro.en: Palace has no prefix or suffix of its own: it is a place name that became a noun, and its derived words are built on that noun.
intro.cn: palace 本身没有前缀或后缀：它是一个变成名词的地名，其派生词都建在这个名词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin Palatium supplied the name, and the adjective palatinus described what belonged to the imperial hill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Palatium 提供了这个名字，形容词 palatinus 描述属于皇帝那座山的事物。

items.structure: Palatium (Latin proper noun, the Palatine hill)
items.example: Palatium named a place before it named a building.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字先指地点，后指建筑。

items.meaning: of the Palatine; of the imperial court
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述一位宫廷官员。

items.example: Old French carried the hill's name to a house.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把山名带到了房子上。

items.example: The flat has a palatial bathroom.
items.exampleCN: 这套公寓有一间宫殿般的浴室。

items.meaning: the territory of a count palatine
items.example: The palatinate had its own courts.
The palazzo opens onto a small square.
items.exampleCN: 这座府邸朝向一个小广场。

items.meaning: a seizure of power from inside the court
items.meaningCN: 由宫廷内部发动的夺权
items.example: A palace coup removed the old guard.
items.exampleCN: 一场宫廷政变清除了旧班底。

latinEntries.meaning: the Palatine hill; the imperial residence
of the Palatine or the court

definition_zh: 苍白的；浅色的；逊色的；变苍白
definition_en: having little colour in the face, light and weak in shade, less impressive than something it is compared with, and to lose colour
core_image: 一张血色退去的脸，像被水冲淡的颜色
scene: 清晨的诊室里，医生抬起病人的手腕，看那张几乎没有血色的脸。The nurse noticed how pale his face had become after the long night.
sceneCN: 这里 pale 是「脸色苍白」（第 1 个义项：脸上缺少血色）；句意为护士注意到他熬过漫长一夜之后脸色变得多么苍白。图中可辨识物件：诊室的灯、病人的手腕、床尾的病历夹。

derivatives.zh: pale 加表示性质的后缀 -ness，指苍白、色淡
pale 加副词后缀 -ly，指苍白地、淡淡地
与 pale 同出拉丁语 pallor，指脸色苍白，多用于书面
与 pale 同出拉丁词干 pallidus，指无血色的、病态的苍白

senses.title: Having little colour in the face
senses.definition: having less colour than usual in the face, often because of illness, fear or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 脸上比平时缺少血色，常因生病、害怕或疲惫
senses.example: She went pale when the results were read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。
senses.why: Latin pallere meant to be pale, and the word has always started from skin losing its healthy colour, so the face is its oldest and most natural subject.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pallere 本义就是发白、失色，这个词最早说的是皮肤失去健康颜色，所以「脸」是它最古老也最自然的落点。

senses.title: Light and weak in shade
senses.definition: of a colour or light, close to white and not strong or deep
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色或光线接近白色，不浓、不深
senses.example: The walls were painted a pale grey.
senses.exampleCN: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。
senses.why: Once the word names a weak version of white, it can describe any colour that has been diluted, which is why pale blue sits nearer white than pure blue.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用来指「被冲淡的白」，就能描述任何掺淡的颜色，所以 pale blue 比纯蓝更靠近白。

senses.title: Weaker than what it is compared with
senses.definition: less impressive, less strong or less real than another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 比同类的另一事物更不打动人、更弱或更不真实
senses.example: The new version is a pale imitation of the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新版本只是对旧版本一种拙劣的模仿。
senses.why: A pale copy lacks the full colour of the original, so the word came to mean anything that looks washed out beside a stronger model.
senses.whyCN: 淡色的复制品没有原件那样饱满的颜色，于是这个词转指任何在更强的样本旁显得褪色、单薄的东西。

senses.title: To lose colour from the face
senses.definition: to become pale, especially in the face, or to make something seem less strong by comparison
senses.definitionCN: 变得苍白，尤指脸色发白；也可指使某物相形之下显得黯淡
senses.example: His cheeks paled at the sight of the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 一看见血，他的双颊就白了。
senses.why: The verb only sets the adjective in motion: the colour leaves the face while others watch it go, so the change itself becomes the event.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把形容词动了起来：血色在旁人眼前从脸上退走，于是「退去」这个变化本身成了一件可以叙述的事。

intro.en: Pale comes from Latin pallere, to be pale, through Old French; the same Latin family gives pallor and pallid, so the colour sense is very old.
intro.cn: pale 出自拉丁语 pallere（发白），经古法语进入英语；同一拉丁词族还给出 pallor 与 pallid，颜色义由来已久。

items.en: The verb pallere meant to be pale or to look colourless, and it described the skin before it described anything else.
items.cn: 动词 pallere 意为发白、没有血色，它最初描述的是皮肤，而不是别的物体。

items.en: Its adjective pallidus meant pale or wan and passed into learned words such as pallid.
items.cn: 它的形容词 pallidus 意为苍白、憔悴，后来进入 pallid 这类书面词。

items.en: Old French turned the Latin adjective into pale, and the form crossed to England with Norman French.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形容词写成 pale，这个形式随诺曼法语一起进入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English used pale for a face without colour and, by extension, for light and washed-out shades.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pale 指没有血色的脸，并由此延伸到浅淡、发白的颜色。

items.en: Modern English keeps paler and palest as the comparison, and adds the figurative sense of a weak or faded copy.
items.cn: 现代英语用 paler 与 palest 作比较级和最高级，并增加了「逊色、褪色的复制品」这一比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the learned relatives that keep the Latin colour stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for a face or a shade that has lost its strength.
note.cn: 形近组收保留拉丁颜色词干的书面亲属词；近义组收描述失去强度的脸色与色调的词。

entries.definition: Pale and unhealthy, especially of a face; it keeps the Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而病态的，尤指脸色；保留了拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being pale, used mostly in medical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的状态，多用于医学文字。

entries.definition: The quality of being pale; pale plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白的性质；pale 加 -ness。

entries.definition: The colour of fresh snow or milk, the lightest shade there is.
entries.definitionCN: 新雪或牛奶的颜色，最浅的色调。

entries.definition: Pale and tired-looking, as if from illness.
entries.definitionCN: 苍白而疲惫的，像病后那样。

entries.definition: Pale grey, like ash, usually of a frightened face.
entries.definitionCN: 灰白的，像灰烬一样，常形容受惊的脸。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for being pale, and everything else in the family returns to a colour that has been drained.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「发白」的动词上，词族里其余的词都回到一种被抽走浓度的颜色。

normal.en: Latin pallere means to be pale, so the word begins at the skin, not at the paint pot.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pallere 意为发白，所以这个词的起点在皮肤，而不在油漆桶。

normal.en: Pallor and pallid are learned relatives that keep the Latin colour sense.
normal.cn: pallor 与 pallid 是保留拉丁颜色义的书面亲属词。

normal.en: A face goes pale, a colour is pale, and a copy looks pale beside the original: one word measures distance from full colour.
normal.cn: 脸会发白，颜色会发淡，复制品在原件旁显得褪色，同一个词量的是离饱满颜色有多远。

normal.en: The verb pale is simply the adjective set in motion while others watch the colour leave.
normal.cn: 动词 pale 只是把形容词动起来，让别人看着颜色退走。

normal.en: Pale blue is not a kind of blue but blue with white mixed in, which is why the word can also mean weak.
normal.cn: pale blue 不是一种蓝，而是掺了白的蓝，所以这个词也能表示「弱」。

abstract.en: Colour is evidence of health, so losing it is the body's first way of saying that something is wrong.
abstract.cn: 颜色是健康的证据，褪色是身体最先说出「不对劲」的方式。

abstract.en: A pale copy is judged against an original it cannot match, which turns the word into a quiet comparison.
abstract.cn: 淡色的复制品总被拿去和配不上的原件相比，这个词因此成了一场安静的对照。

abstract.en: Every pale thing is a full thing with part of its colour taken away.
abstract.cn: 每个发淡的东西，都是被抽走了一部分颜色的完整之物。

examples.en: She went pale when the results were read out.
examples.cn: 结果念出来的时候，她的脸一下子白了。

examples.en: The walls were painted a pale grey.
examples.cn: 墙被刷成了浅浅的灰色。

examples.en: The sequel is a pale copy of the original film.
examples.cn: 这部续集是原片一个褪色的复制品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪」——病人脸色苍白，床边总得有人陪着；记住 pale 是苍白。

root: 拉丁语 pallere（发白）— pallidus（苍白的）— 古法语 pale — 英语 pale；同族书面词有 pallor、pallid。

sensesIntro.en: The core is colour with its strength taken out; the senses move from the face, to light shades, to the figurative weak copy, and finally to the act of losing colour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被抽走浓度的颜色；义项从脸，到浅淡的色彩，再到比喻性的「逊色复制品」，最后回到「失去颜色」这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face whose colour has drained away like paint thinned by water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张血色退去的脸，颜色像被水冲淡的颜料。

branches.en: a patient's face under a clinic lamp
branches.cn: 诊室灯下病人的脸

branches.en: a wall painted a soft grey
branches.cn: 被刷成柔和浅灰的墙

branches.en: a sequel that cannot match the first film
branches.cn: 比不过首部的续集

branches.en: cheeks losing colour at the sight of blood
branches.cn: 见到血时退去血色的脸颊

branches.en: a washed-out colour and a washed-out copy
branches.cn: 褪掉的颜色与褪掉的复制品

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of being pale, its adjective and noun, and English suffixes that turn the quality into a state or a manner.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示发白的动词及其形容词、名词承载，再加上把性质变成状态或方式的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: a verb of being pale, an adjective for the pale colour, and a noun for paleness itself.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族有明确记录：表示发白的动词、指苍白颜色的形容词，以及指苍白本身的名词。

items.meaning: to be pale, to lack colour

definition_zh: 手掌；掌心；棕榈树；把…藏于掌中；骗卖
definition_en: the inner surface of the hand, a tropical tree with a crown of large fanning leaves, and to hide something small in the hand or pass it off on someone
core_image: 一只摊开的手，掌纹向四周散开，像撑开的扇叶
scene: 庙会的老先生摊开手，让围着的孩子看他掌心的纹路。The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
sceneCN: 这里 palm 是「手掌、掌心」（第 1 个义项：手的内侧面）；句意为老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。图中可辨识物件：摊开的手掌、庙会的灯笼、围观的孩子。

collocations.phrase: in the palm of one's hand
collocations.zh: 在某人的掌心里；完全受其掌控

derivatives.zh: palm 加表示「从事某事的人」的后缀 -ist，指看手相的人
palm 加表示技艺的后缀 -istry，指看手相的方术
palm 加 -y 构成，先指多棕榈的，再引申为繁荣兴旺的

senses.title: The inner surface of the hand
senses.definition: the inner surface of the hand, from the wrist to the base of the fingers
senses.definitionCN: 手的内侧面，从手腕一直到手指根部
senses.example: The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
senses.exampleCN: 老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。
senses.why: Latin palma first named this flat, open surface, so the word begins at the body part whenever a hand is held out or turned upward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 palma 最初就指这块平坦、张开的表面，所以只要把手摊开或翻向上，这个词就从身体部位开始。

senses.title: A tropical tree with fanning leaves
senses.definition: a tropical tree with a tall trunk and a crown of large leaves spreading from one point
senses.definitionCN: 一种热带树木，树干高大，大叶子从同一点向四周展开
senses.example: A row of palms shaded the road along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸公路旁一排棕榈树投下阴凉。
senses.why: The fronds of many palms spread from one point like the fingers of an open hand, so Latin reused palma for the tree and English kept both senses.
senses.whyCN: 许多棕榈的叶片从同一点向外张开，像摊开的手指向四周，拉丁语就把 palma 也给了这种树，英语把两个义项都留了下来。

senses.title: To hide something in the hand
senses.definition: to hide a small object in the closed hand, especially to deceive someone
senses.definitionCN: 把一个小东西藏在合起的手里，尤指为了骗人
senses.example: He palmed the coin and slipped it into his sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 他把硬币扣在掌心，顺手滑进了袖口。
senses.why: Once palm names the part of the hand others cannot see when it closes, the verb can name the trick of keeping an object there while everyone watches.
senses.whyCN: 既然 palm 指手合拢后别人看不见的那一面，动词就能指「在众目之下把东西留在那里」的手法。

senses.title: To pass something off on someone
senses.definition: to get rid of something by persuading someone that it is better than it is
senses.definitionCN: 靠让人相信某物比实际更好，从而把东西脱手
senses.example: The dealer palmed off a fake watch on a tourist.
senses.exampleCN: 那个商贩把一块假表骗卖给了游客。
senses.why: The hand that conceals can also pass something on unseen, so palm off names a deal finished before the other person has had a proper look.
senses.whyCN: 会藏东西的手也能把东西悄悄递出去，所以 palm off 指一笔在对方看清之前就已成交的买卖。

intro.en: Palm goes back to Latin palma, which named both the flat of the hand and the tree whose leaves spread like fingers; Old English borrowed it for the tree and the hand.
intro.cn: palm 出自拉丁语 palma，这个词既指手掌的平面，也指叶片像手指一样张开的树；古英语把两个意思都借了进来。

items.en: Palma named the flat inner surface of the hand, the part held open or used to strike.
items.cn: palma 指手内那一块平坦的表面，也就是摊开或用来拍打的那一面。

items.en: The same word was given to the date palm because its fronds fan out from one point like an open hand.
items.cn: 同一个词也被给了枣椰树，因为它的叶丛从同一点张开，像一只摊开的手。

items.en: Old English took the word through the church, first for the palm branches carried on Palm Sunday and then for the tree.
items.cn: 古英语经教会借入这个词，先指棕枝主日所持的棕榈枝，再指这种树。

items.en: Middle English kept the hand sense and the tree sense side by side, and also used palm as a unit of length taken from the hand.
items.cn: 中古英语让「手」与「树」两个义项并存，还把 palm 用作以手宽为准的长度单位。

items.en: Modern English keeps palmed and palming, and the phrase palm off for passing something off on someone.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 palmed 与 palming，以及表示「骗卖、塞给别人」的 palm off。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for the hand and the tree; the near-meaning group gathers words for hands and for the leaves that look like them.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语中兼指手掌与棕榈的那个词展开；近义组收表示手以及像手的叶片的词。

entries.definition: A medieval pilgrim who carried a palm branch home from the Holy Land.
entries.definitionCN: 中世纪从圣地朝圣归来、手持棕榈枝的朝圣者。

entries.definition: A person who reads the lines of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 看手相的人。

entries.definition: The practice of telling a person's future from the lines of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 从手掌纹路推测命运的方术。

entries.definition: The whole part of the body at the end of the arm, fingers included.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂末端包含手指的整个部位。

entries.definition: The foot of an animal such as a dog or cat.
entries.definitionCN: 狗、猫等动物的脚掌。

entries.definition: A long leaf of a palm or a fern, divided into many parts.
entries.definitionCN: 棕榈或蕨类那种分成许多部分的长叶。

normalIntro.en: One Latin word covers the open hand and the tree that copies its shape, and the family around it keeps folding the hand into a tool of hiding.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁词同时覆盖摊开的手与模仿其形状的树，而它周围的词族不断把这只手折成藏东西的工具。

normal.en: Latin palma is both the open hand and the palm tree, one picture doing two jobs.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 palma 既是摊开的手，也是棕榈树，一幅画面干了两件事。

normal.en: The lines of the palm are what palmistry claims to read.
normal.cn: 掌纹正是 palmistry 声称要读的东西。

normal.en: A palm was once a unit of length measured across the hand.
normal.cn: palm 曾是以手宽丈量的长度单位。

normal.en: The verb palm keeps the hand closed: the coin vanishes inside it.
normal.cn: 动词 palm 让手合起来：硬币就在里面不见了。

normal.en: Palm off adds a direction to that closed hand: the hidden thing is pushed onto someone else.
normal.cn: palm off 给这只合起的手加了方向：藏着的东西被推给了别人。

abstract.en: The palm is the part of the body that can both give and conceal.
abstract.cn: 手掌是身体上既能给予又能藏匿的那一部分。

abstract.en: A tree that looks like an open hand ties the body to the landscape.
abstract.cn: 一棵看起来像摊开的手的树，把身体和风景系在一起。

abstract.en: Whatever fits inside a closed palm is small enough to be denied.
abstract.cn: 能握进掌心的东西，小到可以否认它存在。

examples.en: The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
examples.cn: 老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。

examples.en: A row of palms shaded the road along the coast.
examples.cn: 海岸公路旁一排棕榈树投下阴凉。

examples.en: The dealer palmed off a fake watch on a tourist.
examples.cn: 那个商贩把一块假表骗卖给了游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕姆」——摊开手掌喊一声「帕姆」，记住 palm 是手掌。

root: 拉丁语 palma（手掌），同一个词又指棕榈，因叶丛像摊开的手；经古英语 palm 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the open hand; the senses widen to the tree that copies its shape, then narrow to the closed hand that hides and finally to the hand that cheats.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是摊开的手；义项先扩到形状如手的棕榈，再收拢到藏东西的合掌，最后落到行骗的那只手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand whose lines spread outward like the leaves of a fan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手，掌纹向四周散开，像撑开的扇叶。

branches.en: a reader tracing the lines of a palm
branches.cn: 看相人沿掌纹描过去

branches.en: a coast road shaded by tall palms
branches.cn: 被高大棕榈遮荫的海岸公路

branches.en: a coin vanishing inside a closed hand
branches.cn: 硬币在合起的手里消失

branches.en: a fake watch passed to a tourist
branches.cn: 假表被塞给游客

branches.en: leaves that fan out like fingers and a hand that closes
branches.cn: 像手指张开的叶丛与合拢的手

intro.en: The word is a single Latin noun for hand and tree, with English suffixes building the reader, the art and the tree-filled place.
intro.cn: 这个词就是一个兼指手掌与棕榈的拉丁名词，英语后缀在它周围造出看相人、相术和长满棕榈的地方。

latinIntro.en: Latin palma is recorded for both the hand and the tree, and the adjective palmatus describes something shaped or decorated like a hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 palma 兼指手掌与棕榈，形容词 palmatus 则描述像手一样张开或以棕榈装饰的东西。

latinEntries.meaning: palm of the hand; palm tree
shaped like a hand, decorated with palms

definition_zh: 面板；镶板；控制面板；专家小组；陪审团名单；（漫画）分格；固定样本组
definition_en: a flat rectangular piece fitted into a frame or surface; also a group of people selected to sit together and give opinions or make decisions
core_image: 一块绷在框架里的方形板，也可以是一群人选出来坐到同一张长桌后面
scene: 演播室里，四位专家坐在长桌后。A square panel of lights came on above the table, and the host asked the four experts beneath it to begin.
sceneCN: 这里 panel 是「嵌在框架里的平板、灯板」（第 1 个义项：嵌在框架里的平板）；句意：长桌上方一块方形灯板亮起，主持人请坐在它下面的四位专家开始讨论。图中可辨识物件：长桌、四把椅子、专家名牌、方形灯板、麦克风；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: （选出的）专家小组；评审团；讨论组

forms.label: 过去式／过去分词（英式拼写）
过去式／过去分词（美式拼写）

derivatives.zh: 小组成员；评审之一
镶板材料；镶板工程（美式拼写）
装有镶板的（英式拼写）
分面板；子面板；下级小组
小组讨论（复合名词）

senses.title: A flat piece fitted into a frame
senses.definition: a usually rectangular piece of wood, glass, or metal that forms part of a surface or is set into a frame
senses.definitionCN: 通常为矩形的木、玻璃或金属板，构成某个表面的一部分，或嵌在框架里
senses.example: One panel of the door was cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 门上有一块镶板裂了。
senses.why: The word began as the name of a square piece of cloth. A piece cut to fit a frame keeps that shape, so the first modern sense is simply a flat rectangle inserted into a larger surface.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一块方形的布。裁好嵌进框架的一块仍保留那个形状，因此最早的现代义就是“插进更大表面里的一块平板”。

senses.title: The surface you operate: control panel
senses.titleCN: 你操作的那块面：控制面板
senses.definition: a flat surface on a machine or device that holds the controls, dials, or screens
senses.definitionCN: 机器或装置上集中安放控制键、旋钮或屏幕的平面
senses.example: The pilot checked the panel before takeoff.
senses.exampleCN: 起飞前飞行员检查了仪表板。
senses.why: A fitted board is a natural place to mount switches. Once the board carries the controls, the object becomes the interface, and the panel is what the hand reaches for.
senses.whyCN: 嵌装好的板面天然适合安装开关。一旦这块板承载了控制装置，它就成了人机接口，“面板”也就成了手要伸向的那块地方。

senses.title: A selected group at one table
senses.titleCN: 被选出来坐在一起的一组人
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to discuss a subject, judge a competition, or advise on a matter
senses.definitionCN: 被选出来讨论某个议题、评审比赛或提供建议的一组人
senses.example: A panel of judges will review the entries.
senses.exampleCN: 一个评审小组将审阅参赛作品。
senses.why: The group sense grows from a written list of names: a panel was first the sheet on which chosen names were written. The paper gave its name to the people listed on it.
senses.whyCN: “一组人”的义项来自一张写有名字的名单：panel 最初指写着被选中者名字的那张纸。纸的名字后来转移到了纸上所列的人身上。

senses.title: The jury list, and the jury itself
senses.titleCN: 陪审员名单，以及陪审团
senses.definition: the list of people summoned to serve on a jury, or the jury so formed
senses.definitionCN: 被传唤担任陪审员者的名单，或由此组成的陪审团
senses.example: The clerk read the panel aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员在法庭上宣读了陪审员名单。
senses.why: In law the sheet of names came first: the panel was the roll. Then the word shifted to the body of people on the roll, which is the same paper-to-people transfer seen in the expert sense.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，先有那张名单：panel 是名册。随后词义转到名册上的人，这与“专家组”义项中“纸→人”的转移完全相同。

senses.title: A frame in a comic strip
senses.definition: one framed picture or box in a comic strip or graphic novel
senses.definitionCN: 连环画或图像小说中被边框围住的一幅画或一格
senses.example: The final panel shows the empty street.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一格画的是空荡荡的街道。
senses.why: Each comic image is literally a rectangle drawn inside a border, a panel fitted into the page. The printing term for a bordered block transferred to the art form built out of such blocks.
senses.whyCN: 漫画的每一幅画就是画在边框里的一个矩形，即嵌进页面的一块板。印刷业对“带框区块”的叫法，转移到了由这种区块构成的画种上。

senses.title: A solar panel: a board that collects
senses.titleCN: 太阳能板：一块收集能量的板
senses.definition: one of the flat modules that make up a solar array, converting sunlight into electricity
senses.definitionCN: 组成太阳能阵列的平坦模块之一，把阳光转化为电能
senses.example: The roof holds twelve solar panels.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶装了十二块太阳能板。
senses.why: The object is again a flat rectangle mounted into a frame, this time a roof or a rack. What changed is the function: the board no longer covers, it collects.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是嵌在框架（屋顶或支架）里的一块平板。改变的是功能：这块板不再用于遮盖，而是用于收集。

senses.title: A panel show: guests as a group
senses.titleCN: panel show：嘉宾作为一组出场
senses.definition: in broadcasting, a programme in which a group of guests discuss or compete
senses.definitionCN: 广播或电视中由一组嘉宾讨论或竞赛的节目
senses.example: The comedy panel show runs every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这档喜剧小组节目每周五播出。
senses.why: Television keeps the legal and expert group but changes the setting: the panel is now chosen for entertainment, and the group itself becomes the format of the programme.
senses.whyCN: 电视保留了法律与专家义里的“一组人”，却换了场景：panel 现在是为娱乐而挑选的，这一组人本身就成了节目的形式。

senses.title: A fixed sample followed over time
senses.titleCN: 长期追踪的固定样本组
senses.definition: in research, a group of the same people or households surveyed repeatedly over time
senses.definitionCN: 研究中被反复调查、长期追踪的同一批人或家庭
senses.example: The household panel has been interviewed every year since 1990.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭样本组自 1990 年以来每年接受访谈。
senses.why: A panel here is a list that is deliberately kept closed: the same names stay on the roll so that changes can be measured. The legal roll of names becomes a scientific instrument.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 panel 是一份刻意保持封闭的名单：同一批名字始终留在名册上，以便测量变化。法律上的名册于是变成了科学工具。

intro.en: Panel is a small French word for a piece of cloth that grew into a word for boards, lists, and groups. The date of the Latin base is old, but its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: panel 本是法语里指一块布的小词，后来长成指板、名单与群体的词。其拉丁语基础年代久远，但更早来源不确定。

items.en: Panel is recorded meaning 'a piece of cloth, especially a square'. It comes from Old French panel, a diminutive of pan 'piece of cloth'.
items.cn: panel 最早记录于 14 世纪早期，意为“一块布，尤指方形的布”。它来自古法语 panel，是 pan“一块布”的指小形式。

items.en: The legal sense appears: the panel is the schedule or roll of jurors. The sheet of paper is named first; the jury named on it follows later.
items.cn: 法律义出现：panel 指陪审员的名单或名册。先命名那张纸，纸上所列的陪审团随后才被这样称呼。

items.en: The sense 'group of experts' is recorded, again by transfer from a list of selected names to the people themselves.
items.cn: “专家组”义记录于 16 世纪 70 年代，同样是“被选中者的名单”转移到“这些人本身”。

items.en: The wooden architectural sense becomes common: a panel is a board set into wainscot or a door. The verb appears in the 15c. as empanel 'to enter on a roll' and in the 1630s as 'to fit with panels'.
items.cn: 建筑木作义在 1600 年前后普及：panel 是嵌进护墙板或门里的木板。动词 15 世纪出现，作 empanel“列入名册”；17 世纪 30 年代又有“装镶板”义。

items.en: Technology multiplies the board: control panel, instrument panel, solar panel. Media adds the comic panel and the panel show; social science adds the survey panel.
items.cn: 技术让“板”大量增殖：控制面板、仪表板、太阳能板。传媒加上漫画分格与小组节目；社会科学加上调查样本组。

note.en: The first group separates near spellings; the second compares words for organised groups of people.
note.cn: 第一组把形近词分开；第二组比较表示“有组织的一组人”的词。

entries.definition: relating to punishment, especially under the law. One letter differs, and its root is poena 'penalty', not pannus 'cloth'.
entries.definitionCN: 与刑罚有关的，尤指法律上的。只差一个字母，其词根是 poena“惩罚”，不是 pannus“布”。

entries.definition: sudden uncontrolled fear. It looks close but comes from Pan, the Greek god whose sudden appearances caused alarm.
entries.definitionCN: 突如其来的失控恐惧。外形相近，但来自希腊神 Pan——他的突然出现会引发惊惶。

entries.definition: the boards that line a wall, or the work of fitting them. It is the noun from panel, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 墙面上的镶板，或安装镶板的工程。它是 panel 派生的名词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a member of a panel. The -ist suffix marks a person, so it is a true derivative.
entries.definitionCN: 小组或评审组的一员。-ist 后缀标记人，因此它是真正的派生词。

entries.definition: a formally appointed group that meets to decide or manage. It has authority and procedure; a panel is often advisory or judging.
entries.definitionCN: 正式任命、开会决策或管理的团体。它有权力与程序；panel 常是咨询性或评审性的。

entries.definition: the group of people who decide a case in court. A panel can be the list from which the jury is drawn.
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上裁决案件的一组人。panel 可以指从中抽取陪审员的那份名单。

entries.definition: the group that governs a company or institution. It is permanent and powerful, while a panel is usually assembled for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 治理公司或机构的团体。它是常设且有实权的，而 panel 通常为某项任务临时组成。

entries.definition: a meeting or place for open discussion, often with an audience. It stresses exchange; a panel stresses the few selected speakers.
entries.definitionCN: 公开讨论的会议或场所，常有听众。它强调交流；panel 强调被选出的少数发言者。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the board and the table, then three abstract images about selection and framing.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕“板”和“长桌”的挂钩，再用三个关于“遴选与取景”的抽象画面。

normal.en: panel and pane: a window pane is a sheet of glass, and a panel is a sheet fitted into a frame. Same shape, same idea.
normal.cn: panel 与 pane：窗玻璃是一整片，panel 是嵌进框架的一片。形状相同，想法也相同。

normal.en: A control panel is where your fingers walk: buttons arranged on one flat board.
normal.cn: 控制面板是手指行走的地方：按钮排在同一块平板上。

normal.en: Think of a talk show: four chairs behind one long desk. The desk makes the group a panel.
normal.cn: 想一场脱口秀：一张长桌后四把椅子。那张长桌把这一组人变成 panel。

normal.en: A jury panel is first a list on paper, then the people on the paper. Paper first, people second.
normal.cn: 陪审团 panel 先是纸上的一份名单，然后才是名单上的人。先纸，后人。

normal.en: Solar panels are panels that stopped covering walls and started collecting light.
normal.cn: 太阳能板是不再盖墙、改去收集光的面板。

abstract.en: A panel is a frame that decides what counts: the board cuts a piece out of a larger surface and makes it the unit.
abstract.cn: panel 是一个决定“什么算数”的框：它从更大的表面里切出一块，让这块成为单位。

abstract.en: A panel of people is a list made visible: selection is the real subject, and the table is only where the list sits.
abstract.cn: 由人组成的 panel 是一份被看见的名单：真正的主角是“遴选”，长桌只是名单落座的地方。

abstract.en: Every panel hides the rest of the wall. What is outside the frame is as important as what is inside.
abstract.cn: 每一块面板都遮住了墙的其余部分。框外之物与框内之物同样重要。

examples.en: The inspector opened the control panel and found a loose wire.
examples.cn: 检查员打开控制面板，发现一根松动的电线。

examples.en: A panel of three teachers will interview the candidates.
examples.cn: 一个由三位教师组成的小组将面试候选人。

examples.en: The survey follows the same panel of families for ten years.
examples.cn: 这项调查对同一批家庭样本追踪十年。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 pan 记成“一片”，-el 记成“小块”：一片裁好的方板；一群被写进同一张名单的人，也像排在同一块板上。
dict_mnemonic.text: pan（一片布、一片） + -el（指小）→ 嵌板、面板 → 名单 → 坐在名单上的一组人

root: 古法语 panel（一块布）< 通俗拉丁 *pannellus < 拉丁 pannus“布片”；pannus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one object and one list: a fitted square of cloth or wood becomes a control surface, a comic frame, and a solar module; meanwhile a roll of selected names becomes a jury, an expert group, a broadcast format, and a research sample.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项沿着“一块板”和“一份名单”两条线展开：裁好嵌进去的方板变成控制面、漫画格与太阳能模块；而被选中者的名册则变成陪审团、专家组、节目形式与研究样本。

core.en: A square board set into a frame, and a sheet of names laid on a table
core.cn: 一块嵌进框架的方形板，以及一张铺在桌上的名单

branches.en: The board and its working face: a fitted rectangle becomes the place where controls sit.
branches.cn: 板与它的工作面：一块嵌好的矩形变成安放控制装置的地方。

branches.en: The selected group: experts at a table, then guests arranged as a programme format.
branches.cn: 被选出的一组：长桌后的专家，随后被编排成节目形式的嘉宾组。

branches.en: The roll of names: jurors summoned by a list, and a sample kept on a list for years.
branches.cn: 名册：按名单传唤的陪审员，以及多年保留在同一名单上的样本。

branches.en: The framed rectangle as an artistic unit: one bordered picture in a comic strip.
branches.cn: 作为艺术单位的带框矩形：连环画中被边框围住的一格。

branches.en: A board that collects: a solar panel turning sunlight into current.
branches.cn: 一块收集能量的板：把阳光变成电流的太阳能板。

intro.en: Panel has a small but clear family: the base word, its person noun, its material noun, and a few prefixed or compound forms.
intro.cn: panel 的词族不大但很清楚：基词、指人的名词、指材料的名词，以及几个加前缀或复合的形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is pannus 'cloth, rag', with a Vulgar Latin diminutive *pannellus. The further origin of pannus is uncertain, so no deeper root is asserted here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 pannus“布、破布”，其通俗拉丁语指小形式为 *pannellus。pannus 的更早来源不确定，因此这里不强行给出更深词根。

items.meaning: a piece of cloth; later a fitted board or a listed group
items.meaningCN: 一块布；后来指嵌板或名单上的一组人
items.example: The wall was divided into panels.
items.exampleCN: 墙面被分成一块块镶板。
每位小组成员有五分钟。

items.meaning: boards fitted to a wall; the work of fitting them
items.exampleCN: 橡木镶板覆盖了大厅墙面。

items.example: A panelled study faced the garden.
items.exampleCN: 一间镶板书房朝向花园。

items.meaning: a smaller panel within a larger one; a subordinate group
items.meaningCN: 大面板中的分面板；下级小组
items.example: The subpanel reports to the main committee.
items.exampleCN: 下级小组向主委员会汇报。

items.meaning: to enter a person on a jury roll; to form a panel
items.meaningCN: 把某人列入陪审员名册；组成小组
items.exampleCN: 法庭组成了十二人的陪审团。

items.meaning: a piece of cloth (the source of panel)
items.example: Pan in Old French meant a patch of cloth.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 pan 指一块布片。

items.meaning: a single sheet of glass in a frame
items.example: The ball broke a pane of the window.
items.exampleCN: 球打碎了窗户的一块玻璃。

items.meaning: a research design that re-surveys the same sample
items.meaningCN: 对同一样本重复调查的研究设计
items.example: The panel study tracked income for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 该样本研究追踪收入达十年。

latinEntries.meaning: cloth, rag, a piece of fabric
latinEntries.example: Pannus is the base of French pan and English panel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pannus 是法语 pan 与英语 panel 的基础词。

latinEntries.meaning: a small piece of cloth (reconstructed Vulgar Latin)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一小块布（重构的通俗拉丁语形式）
latinEntries.example: Vulgar Latin *pannellus led to Old French panel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 通俗拉丁语 *pannellus 演变为古法语 panel。

definition_zh: 恐慌；惊慌；经济恐慌；惊慌失措
definition_en: a sudden overpowering fear that stops clear thought, a widespread fright in a market or crowd, and to act in such fear
core_image: 灯忽然灭掉的剧场里，人群同时转身挤向同一个门口
scene: 剧场里的灯忽然全灭，前排的人先站起来，后排跟着往门口挤。A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
sceneCN: 这里 panic 是「群体性恐慌」（第 1 个义项：骤然袭来的强烈恐惧）；句意为后排的一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。图中可辨识物件：熄灭的顶灯、挤向出口的人影、翻倒的座椅。

senses.title: A sudden overpowering fear
senses.definition: a sudden, overwhelming feeling of fear that stops people from thinking clearly
senses.definitionCN: 骤然袭来、压倒一切的恐惧，使人无法清楚思考
senses.example: A shout from the back turned the whole crowd into a panic.
senses.exampleCN: 后排一声喊叫让整群人陷入恐慌。
senses.why: The word comes from the god Pan, whose sudden cries in the hills were said to terrify travellers, so the sense begins with fear that arrives with no visible cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自牧神潘，据说他在山野里突然发出的叫声会让旅人惊恐，所以词义一开始就是「找不到明确来由的骤然恐惧」。

senses.title: A widespread fright in a market
senses.definition: a sudden loss of confidence that makes many people sell, withdraw or flee at the same moment
senses.definitionCN: 信心骤然崩塌，使许多人在同一时刻抛售、取钱或逃离
senses.example: A rumour about the bank set off a panic among small savers.
senses.exampleCN: 关于那家银行的传言在小储户中引发了一场恐慌。
senses.why: When many people feel the same sudden fear, the word moves from one heart to a whole market: everyone runs at once, and the running itself makes the danger worse.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时感到同一种骤然的恐惧，这个词就从一颗心移到一个市场：所有人一起奔跑，而奔跑本身又让危险更大。

senses.title: To act with blind fear
senses.definition: to be so frightened that you act without thinking, or to make other people behave that way
senses.definitionCN: 害怕到不假思索地行动，或使别人也这样行动
senses.example: She panicked when she could not find her passport at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 在登机口找不到护照时，她一下子慌了。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into behaviour: the fear takes over the body, and the flailing that follows is the word in action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词变成行为：恐惧接管了身体，随后那阵手忙脚乱就是这个词的具体样子。

intro.en: Panic comes from the Greek god Pan; a sudden terror in lonely places was called panikon deima, the fear sent by Pan, and the word reached English through French.
intro.cn: panic 来自希腊牧神潘；荒野中骤然袭来的恐惧被称作 panikon deima，即「潘送来的恐惧」，这个词经法语进入英语。

items.en: Pan was the god of shepherds and wild country, and a sudden cry in the hills was said to come from him.
items.cn: 潘是牧人与荒野之神，山间突然响起的叫声被说成是他发出的。

items.en: Greek panikon, short for panikon deima, named the sudden terror that seized travellers in lonely places.
items.cn: 希腊语 panikon 是 panikon deima 的简称，指在荒野中突然攫住旅人的恐惧。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as panicus; it is a loan, not an inherited Latin word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊形容词借作 panicus；这是借词，不是拉丁语固有词。

items.en: French panique carried the word into English, where it first named fear without a visible cause.
items.cn: 法语 panique 把这个词带进英语，最初指找不到可见原因的恐惧。

items.en: Modern English uses panic for personal fear and for market runs, and spells the past tense panicked with a k to keep the hard sound.
items.cn: 现代英语用 panic 指个人恐惧与市场挤兑，过去式写作 panicked，加 k 以保住硬音。

normalIntro.en: The word carries the name of a god and the shape of a Greek phrase, and its English forms have to protect one hard sound.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一位神的名字和一句希腊短语的形状，它的英语形式还得护住一个硬音。

normal.en: Pan was said to shout in lonely hills, and panic still means fear with no visible cause.
normal.cn: 据说潘会在荒野里突然叫喊，而 panic 至今仍指找不到可见原因的恐惧。

normal.en: The Greek phrase was panikon deima, the terror of Pan, and English cut it down to one word.
normal.cn: 希腊短语是 panikon deima，即「潘的恐惧」，英语把它压缩成了一个词。

normal.en: Panicked doubles the k so the c keeps its hard sound, unlike the wrong spelling paniced.
normal.cn: panicked 双写 k，让 c 保持硬音，而错误的拼写 paniced 做不到。

normal.en: Panic buying empties shelves before the storm has even arrived.
normal.cn: 恐慌性抢购在风暴还没到之前就把货架清空了。

normal.en: A panic attack is the old flight response running with nothing to run from.
normal.cn: 恐慌发作是古老的逃跑反应在空转，根本没有东西可逃。

abstract.en: Panic is fear that spreads faster than the news that caused it.

abstract.en: A crowd in panic is many people obeying the same blind instruction.
abstract.cn: 陷入恐慌的人群，是许多人在服从同一条看不见的指令。

abstract.en: The god is gone, but the sudden shout in the hills is still inside the word.
abstract.cn: 神已经不在了，但山间那声骤然的喊叫仍留在这个词里。

examples.en: She panicked when she could not find her passport at the gate.

senses.title: The material used for writing
senses.definition: the thin material made from wood pulp or other fibres, used for writing, printing and wrapping
senses.definitionCN: 用木浆或其他纤维制成的薄材料，用于书写、印刷和包装
senses.example: He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。
senses.why: The word began as papyrus, the Egyptian reed pressed into sheets, so the material itself is the oldest and most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是 papyrus，即埃及的那种芦苇，压成薄片用来书写，所以「材料」本身就是最古老、最字面的义项。

senses.title: A newspaper
senses.definition: a set of printed sheets published daily or weekly with news and comment
senses.definitionCN: 每日或每周出版、刊载新闻与评论的一套印刷纸张
senses.example: She reads the paper on the train every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上在火车上看报纸。
senses.why: A newspaper is literally paper that carries news, so English kept the material's name for the daily object and dropped the first half of the compound.
senses.whyCN: 报纸字面上就是「载着新闻的纸」，英语把这个日刊直接叫作纸，省掉了复合词的前一半。

senses.title: A written study or an exam
senses.definition: a piece of academic writing on one topic, or the set of questions used in an examination
senses.definitionCN: 就一个题目写成的学术文章，或考试所用的一整套题目
senses.example: He published a paper on coastal erosion last year.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年发表了一篇关于海岸侵蚀的论文。
senses.why: A paper is a piece of writing that exists on paper; scholars hand in such sheets and examiners set them, so the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 论文就是写在纸上的一份文字；学者交上这样的纸页，出题人发出的也是这样的纸页，同一个词就同时覆盖了两边。

senses.title: Official documents
senses.definition: papers, the documents that prove who you are or what you are allowed to do
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 papers，指证明身份或获准做某事的文件
senses.example: The guard asked to see her papers at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 边检人员要求看她的证件。
senses.why: Identity and permission are proved by printed sheets, so the plural papers came to mean the documents a person must carry.
senses.whyCN: 身份与许可都靠印好的纸页来证明，于是复数 papers 就指一个人必须随身携带的那些文件。

senses.title: Made of paper; existing only on paper
senses.titleCN: 纸做的；只停留在纸面上的
senses.definition: made of paper, or true only in written records and not in real life
senses.definitionCN: 用纸做的；或只在书面记录中成立、在现实中并不成立
senses.example: They handed out paper cups at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在入口处发放纸杯。
senses.why: When something exists only as figures on a sheet, it is paper in the adjective's sense: it looks solid but has no body behind it.
senses.whyCN: 当某样东西只以纸上的数字存在时，它就是这个形容词意义上的 paper：看上去实在，背后却没有实体。

intro.en: Paper is named after papyrus, the reed of the Nile; Greek papuros passed into Latin as papyrus and into English through Old French papier.
intro.cn: paper 得名于尼罗河的纸莎草；希腊语 papuros 进入拉丁语作 papyrus，又经古法语 papier 进入英语。

items.en: Papuros was the Egyptian reed whose pith was pressed into writing sheets, and Greek used the same word for the sheets.
items.cn: papuros 是埃及的芦苇，其茎髓被压成书写用的薄片，希腊语也用同一个词指这些薄片。

items.en: Latin took papyrus from Greek for both the plant and the writing material sold across the empire.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借来 papyrus，同时指这种植物和在帝国各地出售的书写材料。

items.en: Old French papier named the material, and Norman scribes brought the word to England.
items.cn: 古法语 papier 指这种材料，诺曼抄写员把这个词带到了英格兰。

items.en: Middle English paper covered the sheets and, as printing spread, the newspaper and the written study.
items.cn: 中古英语的 paper 指纸页，随着印刷术传播，也指报纸与写成的研究。

items.en: Modern English keeps papers for documents and adds paper as an adjective for anything that exists only on a page.
items.cn: 现代英语用 papers 指文件，并把 paper 用作形容词，指只存在于纸面上的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the reed, the material and the things made from it; the near-meaning group gathers other words for sheets and written records.
note.cn: 形近组沿芦苇、材料以及用它做成的东西展开；近义组收其他表示纸页与书面记录的词。

entries.definitionCN: 用压制芦苇制成的古代书写材料，正是 paper 得名的来源。

entries.definition: Thin, dry and light, like paper.
entries.definitionCN: 薄、干、轻，像纸一样。

entries.definition: A printed publication of news, literally news on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 刊载新闻的印刷出版物，字面就是印在纸上的新闻。

entries.definition: A book with a thin flexible cover rather than a hard one.
entries.definitionCN: 用薄软封面而非硬壳装订的书。

entries.definition: A single flat piece of paper, cloth or other thin material.
entries.definitionCN: 纸、布等薄材料的单张平面。

entries.definition: An official record of information, now often kept as a computer file.
entries.definitionCN: 信息的正式记录，如今常以电子文件形式保存。

entries.definition: A periodical publishing scholarly articles in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一领域刊载学术文章的期刊。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the name of a reed, survived as the name of the sheet, and then lent itself to everything printed on that sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一种芦苇的名字，后来成为纸页的名字，再借给写在纸页上的一切。

normal.en: Papyrus was a Nile reed, and paper keeps its name even after the reed was replaced by rags and wood pulp.
normal.cn: papyrus 是一种尼罗河芦苇，即使原料早已换成破布与木浆，paper 仍留着它的名字。

normal.en: A newspaper is literally paper that carries news, which is why the material's name survived in the daily.
normal.cn: 报纸字面上就是载着新闻的纸，所以「材料」的名字留在了这份日刊里。

normal.en: Papers in the plural means documents, the sheets you must show at a border.
normal.cn: 复数 papers 指文件，也就是在边境必须拿出来给人看的那几张纸。

normal.en: A paper can be a study you publish, because scholarship once travelled as printed sheets.
normal.cn: paper 也可以指你发表的论文，因为学问曾经就靠印好的纸页传播。

normal.en: On paper marks a plan that has not yet met the world.
normal.cn: on paper 标出一个还没和现实碰面的计划。

abstract.en: Paper is a surface that holds a thought longer than a voice can.
abstract.cn: 纸是一种表面，能让一个想法留存得比声音更久。

abstract.en: A sheet is cheap, which is why it can carry both a shopping list and a treaty.
abstract.cn: 一张纸很便宜，所以它既能承载购物清单，也能承载条约。

abstract.en: To say something is only on paper is to doubt whether the page can change anything.
abstract.cn: 说某件事只停留在纸面上，就是在怀疑这页纸能否改变任何东西。

examples.en: He pushed the paper aside and started again on a clean sheet.
examples.cn: 他把那张纸推到一边，重新拿一张干净的纸从头写起。

examples.en: He published a paper on coastal erosion last year.
examples.cn: 他去年发表了一篇关于海岸侵蚀的论文。

examples.en: The deal looked good on paper but failed in practice.
examples.cn: 这笔交易在纸面上看着不错，实际操作却失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩珀」——像胡椒一样又薄又轻的一张，一吹就飘走；记住 paper 是纸。

root: 希腊语 papuros（纸莎草）— 拉丁语 papyrus — 古法语 papier — 英语 paper。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the sheet you can write on; the senses then move to the daily printed sheet, the study written on it, the documents you carry, and finally the adjective for what exists only there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是可以书写的纸页；义项随后转到每日印出的那张纸、写在上面的研究、随身携带的文件，最后是「只存在于纸上」的形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of white sheets under a lamp, edges soft from being turned.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下一叠白纸，边角因反复翻动而发毛。

branches.en: a blank sheet waiting under a lamp
branches.cn: 台灯下等着的空白纸

branches.en: a folded daily on a train seat
branches.cn: 火车座位上折起的日报

branches.en: a printed study with a long reference list
branches.cn: 印着长串参考文献的研究论文

branches.en: passports checked at a border desk
branches.cn: 边检台上被查验的护照

branches.en: a cup made of paper and a promise made of ink
branches.cn: 纸做的杯子与墨水写成的承诺

intro.en: The word travels from a Greek reed name through Latin and French, and English then builds compounds that name the things printed on the sheet.
intro.cn: 这个词从希腊语的芦苇名出发，经拉丁语和法语转手，英语再用它造出指纸上各类印刷物的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin papyrus is itself a borrowing from Greek papuros, and it names both the reed and the writing material made from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 papyrus 本身借自希腊语 papuros，兼指这种芦苇和用它制成的书写材料。

definition_zh: 游行；阅兵；炫耀；列队行进
definition_en: an organized public procession, a formal march of troops for inspection, a display meant to impress, and the act of marching in such a group
core_image: 彩旗在前，鼓点整齐，一条街被队伍填满
scene: 国庆那天的长街上，鼓乐队走在最前面，人群挤在两侧挥手。The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
sceneCN: 这里 parade 是「游行」（第 1 个义项：庆祝性的公众行进）；句意为全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。图中可辨识物件：彩旗、鼓、街道两侧的人群。

derivatives.zh: 由 parade 加 -ing 构成，指列队行进或刻意展示的行为
由 parade 加 -er 构成，指参加游行的人，也指爱炫耀的人
由 parade 与 ground 复合而成，指士兵操练、受阅的场地

senses.title: A public procession
senses.definition: an organized public march or procession, often with music, costumes and decorated vehicles, held to celebrate an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的公众行进，常配音乐、服装与彩车，用来庆祝某个日子
senses.example: The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。
senses.why: The word is generally traced through French to a Spanish noun for the place where soldiers halted and formed up; from troops gathering in the street it widened to any organized procession.
senses.whyCN: 一般认为这个词经法语来自西班牙语中表示「士兵停下集合之处」的名词；从军队在街上集合，词义扩大为任何有组织的公众行进。

senses.title: A formal march of troops
senses.definition: a ceremony in which soldiers march in formation past a reviewing officer or a public stand
senses.definitionCN: 士兵列队走过检阅官或观礼台的仪式
senses.example: The general watched the parade from a raised platform.
senses.exampleCN: 将军站在检阅台上观看阅兵。
senses.why: Since the earliest parade was simply soldiers standing ready in one place, the military review is the oldest thread, and flags and formation still carry the sense of being inspected.
senses.whyCN: 既然最早的 parade 只是士兵在一处站好待命，阅兵就是最古老的一条线；旗帜与队形至今仍带着「接受检阅」的意味。

senses.title: A display meant to impress
senses.definition: an ostentatious show of wealth, skills or opinions intended to impress other people
senses.definitionCN: 为给人留下印象而摆出的财富、本领或主张
senses.example: His charity work was a parade of good intentions rather than real help.
senses.exampleCN: 他的慈善活动只是把好意摆出来给人看，并没有真正帮上忙。
senses.why: A procession exists to be watched, so when the watching matters more than the marching, the word slides into showing off.
senses.whyCN: 游行本来就是给人看的，一旦「被看见」比「行进」本身更重要，这个词就滑向了炫耀。

senses.title: To march in formation
senses.definition: to walk or march in an ordered group, especially as part of a ceremony or in order to be seen
senses.definitionCN: 排成整齐的队伍行走，尤指作为仪式的一部分或为了被人看见
senses.example: The children paraded around the playground with paper flags.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们举着纸旗在操场上列队走了一圈。
senses.why: The verb simply sets the procession moving: the same ordered line, now seen as an action instead of a spectacle.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是让那支队伍动起来：同样整齐的一列，从眼前的场面变成了正在进行的动作。

intro.en: Parade is usually traced through French to a Spanish noun for a halting place, with the Latin verb parare, to make ready, at the far end; the showy sense came later.
intro.cn: 一般认为 parade 经法语上溯到西班牙语中表示「停下之处」的名词，最远处是拉丁语动词 parare（准备、使就绪）；「炫耀」义出现得较晚。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare or make ready, and its family spread through the Romance languages with senses of stopping and standing.
items.cn: parare 意为准备、使就绪，这一族词在罗曼语中扩散，带上停下、站定的意思。

items.en: Spanish parada named a halt or the place where troops stopped and formed up, from the verb parar, to stop.
items.cn: 西班牙语 parada 指停下的动作或士兵停下集合的地方，来自动词 parar（停下）。

items.en: French took the word as parade and used it for a setting out of troops and for a showy display.
items.cn: 法语借入后写作 parade，用来指军队列队出场，也指铺张的展示。

items.en: English borrowed parade for a military muster and for the ground where soldiers assembled.
items.cn: 英语借入 parade，指军队集合检阅，也指士兵集合的场地。

items.en: Modern English keeps the military review, the civic procession and the showy display, and uses the verb for marching and for showing off.
items.cn: 现代英语保留阅兵、市民游行与炫耀三层意思，动词则用于列队行进和炫耀。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Spanish and Latin words behind the term, plus two spellings that only resemble it; the near-meaning group follows processions, marches and displays.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个词背后的西班牙语与拉丁语词展开，另收两个只是拼写相像的词；近义组收游行、行进与展示。

entries.definition: A halt, or the place where troops stand ready; the Spanish noun behind the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 停下，或士兵站好待命之处；英语词背后的西班牙语名词。

entries.definition: To stop or to halt, the verb that produced the noun parada.
entries.definitionCN: 停下、止住，是造出名词 parada 的动词。

entries.definition: A comic imitation of a style or a work; it merely looks like parade and comes from other roots.
entries.definitionCN: 对某种风格或作品的滑稽模仿；只是拼写与 parade 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A typical example or a pattern of thinking; the spelling is close but the Greek roots are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 典型范例或思维模式；拼写相近，但希腊词根与 parade 无关。

entries.definition: A line of people or vehicles moving forward as part of a ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 仪式中向前行进的一队人或车辆。

entries.definition: To walk with regular steps, especially as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 有节奏地行走，尤指成群行进。

entries.definition: A public show with costumes and scenes, often outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 常为户外的、带服装与场景的公众表演。

entries.definition: An arrangement or show intended to be looked at.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出来供人观看的展示。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a place where troops stood ready and became a line of people made to be watched; the family around it keeps those two ideas.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从士兵站好待命的地方开始，变成一列特意给人看的队伍；周围的词族一直带着这两个念头。

normal.en: The word is generally traced to Spanish parada, a halt where troops formed up, so the military sense is the oldest.
normal.cn: 一般认为这个词来自西班牙语 parada，即部队停下集合之处，所以军事义最古老。

normal.en: French parade added the idea of a show, which is why a fashion parade is about being watched rather than walking.
normal.cn: 法语 parade 加进了「展示」的意思，所以 fashion parade 的重点是被看，而不是走路。

normal.en: The verb is regular: parades, paraded, parading, with no change of vowel.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：parades、paraded、parading，元音不变。

normal.en: On parade means soldiers are lined up for inspection, not simply walking down a street.
normal.cn: on parade 指士兵列队接受检阅，并不是单纯在街上走。

normal.en: To rain on someone's parade is to spoil a moment that was arranged to be enjoyed in public.
normal.cn: rain on someone's parade 就是破坏一个本来要当众享受的时刻。

abstract.en: A parade turns a street into a stage, and everyone on it is at once performer and audience.
abstract.cn: 游行把街道变成舞台，走在上面的人既是演员也是观众。

abstract.en: A show of strength is still a show, and the word keeps that suspicion that display is not the same as substance.
abstract.cn: 力量的展示终究还是展示，这个词一直保留着「排场不等于实力」的疑虑。

abstract.en: Soldiers standing ready and a band walking past share one name because both are meant to be seen by someone in authority.
abstract.cn: 站好待命的士兵与走过的乐队共用一个词，因为两者都要让有权看的人看见。

examples.en: The whole town turned out to watch the parade pass the old town hall.
examples.cn: 全城人都出来看队伍经过旧市政厅。

examples.en: The general watched the parade from a raised platform.
examples.cn: 将军站在检阅台上观看阅兵。

examples.en: The children paraded around the playground with paper flags.
examples.cn: 孩子们举着纸旗在操场上列队走了一圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕累的」——游行队伍走得太久也会怕累的；记住 parade 是游行。

root: 一般认为经法语 parade 来自西班牙语 parada（停下集合之处），源于拉丁语 parare（准备、使就绪）：士兵站好待命的地方，后来成了给人看的队伍。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an ordered line of people meant to be seen; the senses run from a civic celebration to a military review, to a showing off, and finally to the act of marching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一列特意给人看的整齐队伍；义项从市民庆祝走到阅兵、炫耀，最后落到列队行进这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a band and a line of marchers filling the street while the crowd leans forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓乐队与一列行进的队伍占满街道，人群向前倾身观看。

branches.en: a band leading children down the main street
branches.cn: 鼓乐队带着孩子走过主街

branches.en: soldiers in step before a reviewing stand
branches.cn: 士兵在检阅台前齐步走过

branches.en: a borrowed car shown off at a party
branches.cn: 聚会上炫耀借来的车

branches.en: paper flags waving above a playground
branches.cn: 操场上挥动的纸旗

branches.en: boots striking the ground in one rhythm
branches.cn: 靴子以同一个节奏踏在地上

intro.en: The word is a Romance borrowing, and the pieces that built it are a Latin verb of preparing, a Spanish noun of halting, and a French noun of showing.
intro.cn: 这个词是罗曼语借词，构成它的部件是一个表示准备的拉丁动词、一个表示停下的西班牙名词和一个表示展示的法语名词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin verb is recorded behind this word: parare, to make ready, which passed into Spanish as parar and gave the noun parada.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有一个可考的拉丁动词 parare（准备、使就绪），它进入西班牙语成为 parar，并造出名词 parada。

items.meaning: a show, a setting out of troops
the act of marching or showing off
items.meaningCN: 列队行进或炫耀的行为
